question.problem:
Consider the function $y=\sqrt{({x}^{2}+6x){sin}^{2}⁡x}.$  The derivative of this function for $x\in (0,\pi )$ is given by

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{g(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+h(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+6x}}.
$$

Find the function $g(x)+h(x).$
question.worked_solution:
Our function can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+6x){sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\sqrt{{x}^{2}+6x}\cdot \sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =({x}^{2}+6x)^{1/2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the product and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+6x)^{1/2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{2}+6x)^{1/2})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+6x)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+6x}\cdot (2x+6)+\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{x+3}{{x}^{2}+6x}+\operatorname{cot}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{x+3}{{x}^{2}+6x}+\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=\sqrt{({x}^{2}+6x){sin}^{2}⁡x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+6x){sin}^{2}⁡x}(\frac{x+3}{{x}^{2}+6x}+\operatorname{cot}⁡x) \\  & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+6x){sin}^{2}⁡x}(\frac{x+3}{{x}^{2}+6x}+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}) \\  & =\sqrt{({x}^{2}+6x){sin}^{2}⁡x}(\frac{(x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+({x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{({x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{sin}⁡x}) \\  & =\frac{|\operatorname{sin}⁡x|}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\frac{(x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+({x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+6x}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Given that $x\in (0,\pi ),$ then $|\operatorname{sin}⁡x|=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ so the fraction $\frac{|\operatorname{sin}⁡x|}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}$ simplifies to $1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{(x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+({x}^{2}+6x)\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+6x}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x)+h(x)=x+3+{x}^{2}+6x={x}^{2}+7x+3.
$$
